rationale: The acceptance behavior is sufficiently specified by the story and its authoritative documents. Existing deterministic refresh tests cover much of the controlled workflow, while the required real-data browser timing and equivalence runs are explicit acceptance procedures and cannot be replaced by mocked tests. No new test files were prepared: the remaining harness work is conditional on implementation and should receive focused tests if the harness is extended.

acceptance_checks.expected: For each required cache state, record the production browser build revision, environment, effective settings, data counts, individual first-startup and repeat-navigation readings, and maximum. Use real PostgreSQL data and default All scope; disclose no credentials or private contents.
acceptance_checks.verification: Run the explicit real-data browser procedure from TEST_STRATEGY.md sections 34 and 35.2. Record the exact command, cache state, effective settings from the backend echo or rendered control, and per-run evidence in the story Result.

acceptance_checks.expected: For fresh inputs, expired account inputs, expired Trading Post quotes, and both expired, the initial complete usable cached page finishes within 7000 ms. Completion includes the full requested result set, required controls, a successful displayed-value read, and quiescence associated with the initial calculation context and captured input versions. A placeholder or first visible row does not count.
acceptance_checks.verification: Use real-browser navigation-to-complete-page timing for each cache state. Keep later replacement measurements separate from the initial interval and report unavailable cached-page cases as readiness wait plus eventual completion, not seven-second compliance.

acceptance_checks.expected: For each refresh cycle, report refresh start-to-terminal outcome, refreshed calculation/rendering, and navigation-to-final-result separately. Verify final captured inputs are fresh and the indicator ends only after the final result is rendered. No numeric refresh-speed threshold is implied.
acceptance_checks.verification: Correlate browser observations with calculation context, input versions, task-status outcomes, and final backend freshness metadata. Report observed durations without treating them as an additional budget.

acceptance_checks.expected: Overlapping insufficient-scope account work, changed Trading Post demand, missing inputs, and failure/timeout recovery retain a usable cached result when available and terminate recovery boundedly. Controlled-boundary checks are labeled separately from real-data timings.
acceptance_checks.verification: Reuse the existing deterministic application and browser refresh/recovery regressions. For real-data runs, record each scenario and distinguish no-cache readiness wait from cached-page timing; do not mutate or replace the user's database.

acceptance_checks.expected: Provisional and final results preserve complete economic/domain outputs, with no truncation, fee/ownership/quantity changes, or frontend recalculation. Final replacement preserves valid settings and view state, and row/detail versions remain compatible.
acceptance_checks.verification: Use the implementation reference and unchanged-snapshot real-database HTTP/application equivalence procedure. Compare every result field and row, and inspect controlled refresh regressions for preserved controls, selection, and row/detail compatibility.

acceptance_checks.expected: The Result reports evidence, limitations, breaches or unavailable access, and explicit assessment of QUALITY-005 F1/F2/F5 and PERF-003 F001/F002. It does not declare phase completion, waive criteria, or restore manual acceptance.
acceptance_checks.verification: Review the recorded measurements and scenario results against each cited finding and the resolved UD-013/UD-015 requirements. Keep planner closure authority and any unresolved finding visible.

invariants: A result and its freshness metadata describe the same captured calculation context and input versions; later live markers cannot be substituted.
The initial cached-result interval ends based on quiescence within its own calculation context and is not extended by subsequent refresh replacement.
A usable stale result remains a complete ordinary domain result; expiry alone does not degrade or remove it.
Final status requires fresh required account inputs, covered Trading Post demand, and a calculation completed on those captured inputs.
A missing input is not represented as a fabricated source, zero-cost quote, or invented result.
Refresh failure or timeout preserves the last usable result, terminates visible recovery, and exposes retry where applicable.
Displayed results are complete and economically equivalent; frontend display does not recalculate backend values.
Valid settings, filters, sorting, and selections survive replacement; displayed detail corresponds to compatible row inputs and settings.
Real-database acceptance runs are read-only and do not seed, truncate, or replace user data.
existing_tests_reviewed: frontend/scripts/profit-page-perf.mjs — real-browser navigation timing, quiescence, row interaction, request counts, and effective settings; current observation tracks calculation counts and basic displayed state but does not separate cached-result contexts, captured input versions, or refresh phases.

frontend/scripts/profit-refresh-browser-smoke.mjs — controlled browser lifecycle scenarios for cached, replaced, failed refresh responses, indicator behavior, preserved controls/selection, and retry; explicitly does not establish real backend sequences or refresh timing.
src/test/java/application/CachedCraftingProfitServiceTest.java — deterministic freshness matrix and cached-result behavior with held refresh gateways.
src/test/java/application/CraftingProfitInputCaptureEquivalenceIT.java — real-database captured-input/application equivalence coverage; explicit run, not a default test.
src/test/java/web/CraftingProfitApiRealDbEquivalenceIT.java — real-database HTTP/application result equivalence; explicit run, compares real result data.
src/test/java/uiverify/CraftingProfitPageLoadRealDbPerfIT.java — legacy JavaFX real-database timing precedent; does not measure the active browser UI or cached refresh contract.
docs/QUALITY_METRICS.md — latest supplied measured snapshot is dated 2026-10-03 at an older revision; package coverage values are not a current baseline and are not inferred for this story.
test_specifications: If the browser measurement harness is extended, add focused automated checks proving that a scripted later replacement with identical displayed values but a different calculation context/input version is excluded from the initial completion timestamp and measured separately through final rendering.

If the harness is extended, add a controlled transition test in which a loading placeholder or first row appears before the complete result; assert the measurement does not finish until all requested rows and required controls are present, a displayed-value interaction succeeds, and the initial context is quiescent.

If the harness is extended, assert effective settings and input-version/context metadata are captured from the actual backend response or rendered state for the measured request, and that missing metadata fails the evidence check rather than silently passing.

Run explicit real-browser timing against real PostgreSQL data for fresh account/TP inputs, expired account inputs, expired TP quotes, and both expired; capture startup and repeat navigation separately, full requested output, per-reading times, maximum, environment, revision, data counts, settings, and cache state.

Run controlled-boundary correctness scenarios for overlapping insufficient-scope account work and changed TP demand, missing source/quotes, failure, timeout, and retry. Assert retained cached results where available, bounded visible termination, indicator termination, and preserved settings/view state. Keep these control-flow checks explicitly separate from real-data timing claims.

Run unchanged-snapshot HTTP/application equivalence against real data for the relevant settings, comparing complete ordered results and all authoritative values, blocked state, and missing-material maps. Keep private real-data comparison references outside version control.
Review the completed evidence against QUALITY-005 F1/F2/F5 and PERF-003 F001/F002, recording what this story resolves, what remains unresolved, and any breach or unavailable environment.

pre_implementation_verification.command: Not run. No new tests were prepared; the explicit real-data browser and equivalence procedures require the production browser build and accessible real PostgreSQL environment.

coverage_review: The available QUALITY_METRICS snapshot is from 2026-10-03 at an older revision and is provisional, not a clean baseline. It reports Java application 93.82% line / 71.25% branch and web 93.68% / 82.59%; frontend crafting 94.02% / 85.63%. These historical values do not establish current coverage. No current report was available to verify harness coverage. Do not add tests to raise coverage; if measurement code changes, review the affected report and targeted harness tests as the story requires.
post_implementation_review_reason: Required acceptance depends on explicit real-browser measurements against real user PostgreSQL data and real-data equivalence. Controlled regressions cannot establish the timing budget or prove the live backend produces the measured refresh sequence. Review the recorded runs, version separation, complete-result evidence, equivalence, and finding dispositions after implementation.

post_implementation_reviews.reason: The updated timing tests and recorded runs address context attribution and report separate refresh figures, but the two evaluator gaps remain. The real-browser displayed-value read and enabled-selection check still occur only after the measurement loop has followed refresh to its terminal outcome, so they do not prove the initial cached result was interactive before its timing boundary. Refresh start-to-terminal is still inferred from the initial response and stale-indicator disappearance; task-status bodies and terminal task outcomes are not captured or correlated, and indicator termination is not verified against final rendering.
evidence: frontend/scripts/profit-page-perf.mjs performs the displayed-value read and selection check after following a provisional opening through refresh; the interaction is not part of initial completion eligibility.

frontend/scripts/profitTiming.mjs derives refresh terminal time from the first sample where the stale indicator is gone and identifies replacement from a final calculation context; this does not establish the advertised work's task outcome.

target/perf004-fresh.log, perf004-expired-account.log, perf004-expired-tp.log, and perf004-both-expired.log record timing runs and reported maxima, but those measurements cannot resolve the interactivity and refresh-task evidence gaps.

target/perf004-controlled-frontend.log records 60 passing frontend tests; target/perf004-controlled-backend.log records 28 passing backend tests. target/perf004-equivalence-http.log and perf004-equivalence-capture.log record passing real-database equivalence runs. These support their scoped checks but do not establish the unmet AC2/AC3 evidence.
actionable_items: For provisional openings, perform the displayed-value read and enabled-selection check while the initial calculation context is displayed, and include both in completion eligibility. Add a regression where only the final replacement is interactive, then repeat affected real-browser measurements.

Capture refresh start and terminal task-status outcomes, correlated with the advertised work. Measure refresh execution separately from final calculation/rendering, verify the indicator ends only after the final result is rendered, add focused regressions for those event distinctions, and repeat affected measurements and Result claims.

post_implementation_reviews.reason: The reported initial-page maxima are under 7,000 ms, but the run logs do not establish that the required interactive read occurred within those measured intervals. For example, expired-TP opening #5 reports the initial usable page at 4,316 ms while its completing-sample read is at 7,442 ms and live read at 8,513 ms. Since AC2 includes a successful displayed-value read in completion, this run does not prove the budget was met. The revised refresh attribution, controlled checks, and equivalence evidence address the prior review gaps but do not resolve this timing evidence gap.
evidence: target/perf004-expired-tp-s3.log reports a 4,316 ms initial completion, but the corresponding completing-sample read is at 7,442 ms.
The expired-TP summary's reported maximum is 4,316 ms; its per-opening figures do not incorporate the later read timestamp.
The supplied run logs report task-status outcomes, separate refresh/render timings, final freshness, and successful controlled and equivalence checks, supporting those scoped criteria.
actionable_items: Make the successful displayed-value read and enabled-selection check part of the timed initial completion boundary, with their timestamps tied to the initial context. Rerun affected real-browser measurements and update the maxima and Result claims.

post_implementation_reviews.reason: The recorded evidence supports the acceptance criteria and resolves the two prior QA gaps. The timing harness now includes a successful displayed-value read and enabled-selection check in the initial completion boundary, and correlates refresh outcomes with advertised tasks. The recorded real-browser runs report a maximum of 5,145 ms across the four required cache states; scoped controlled tests and real-database equivalence runs support the other criteria. Limitations and unavailable failure/no-cache scenarios are disclosed. No CI result was required for this review.
evidence: The QA plan has no prepared test paths; the story records 42 focused timing tests and controlled mutation runs that fail when boundary attribution or interactivity checks are broken.
The current timing implementation and its tests cover complete-result eligibility, context separation, interactivity, task-status correlation, and final-render/indicator checks.
The four s5 browser logs report exit=0 and maxima below 7,000 ms, with effective settings, scope, and task outcomes recorded.
The story records passing controlled backend/frontend checks and real-database HTTP/application and captured-input equivalence runs.
The story assesses QUALITY-005 F1/F2/F5 and PERF-003 F001/F002, and discloses that no-cache and live refresh failure/timeout scenarios were unavailable.
